cars.summary: The Nova SS embodies Chevrolet’s compact-muscle formula, pairing a V8 sports package with front disc brakes and strengthened suspension in a relatively small road coupe. Its established place in American performance-car history is reflected in Chevrolet’s dedicated Sports Department catalogue. One original model-generation entry is admitted for the SS engineering package, rather than simply its badges, optional engines or paint.

facts.title: Why this car belongs
facts.explanation: The Nova SS embodies Chevrolet’s compact-muscle formula, pairing a V8 sports package with front disc brakes and strengthened suspension in a relatively small road coupe. Its established place in American performance-car history is reflected in Chevrolet’s dedicated Sports Department catalogue. One original model-generation entry is admitted for the SS engineering package, rather than simply its badges, optional engines or paint.

cars.variant: Eliminator 302 H.O. four-speed — 1970 Ford AMA specification reference
cars.specification_market: Ford-prepared 1970 Cougar Eliminator 302 AMA sheets, model 65 hardtop. Selected cover/dimension/power-team/engine pages visually read, not all 29 pages. Power corrected as stated in the sheet to 60 F and 29.92 in Hg; no modern net/gross label is invented. Compression differs between nominal power-team and maximum engine rows, so is omitted. Axle/Traction-Lok availability is not resolved here. Other engines, XR-7s, convertible recreations and dealer-installed spoilers add no counts.
cars.summary: The Cougar Eliminator is Mercury’s distinctive contribution to the pony-car performance era. The Boss 302 road configuration combined a high-output small-block V8 with a required four-speed in the Cougar’s own hardtop body and longer-wheelbase layout. This mechanical identity and established performance-package history justify one original Cougar family entry; spoilers, colours and alternative engines do not create additional cars.

facts.title: Why this car belongs
facts.explanation: The Cougar Eliminator is Mercury’s distinctive contribution to the pony-car performance era. The Boss 302 road configuration combined a high-output small-block V8 with a required four-speed in the Cougar’s own hardtop body and longer-wheelbase layout. This mechanical identity and established performance-package history justify one original Cougar family entry; spoilers, colours and alternative engines do not create additional cars.
